patient.history: An 87-year-old woman reports breathlessness with exertion that has gradually worsened over the past several months. She now becomes short of breath while walking short distances and improves with rest. She denies chest pain or breathlessness at rest.

REFERRAL LETTER
Date: 09/23/2026
Patient Name: Janet Reed
DOB: 04/10/1939
MRN: MRN-32549

To: Cardiology Clinic Intake
From: Dr. Brian Moore, Summit Family Practice

Dear Colleague,

Reason for referral: Evaluation of breathlessness on exertion.

Janet Reed is an 87-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She reports gradually worsening breathlessness with exertion over the past several months and now becomes short of breath when walking short distances. Symptoms improve with rest.

She denies chest pain or breathlessness at rest. Please evaluate her exertional breathlessness and advise on further care.

Thank you for seeing this patient.

Dr. Brian Moore
Summit Family Practice

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Hypertension, stable by history. Continue the established care plan. Encourage reduced-salt eating and periodic home blood pressure tracking.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stable by history. Continue the established care plan and dietary guidance. Encourage regular activity, home glucose tracking, and routine foot care.

2. Hypertension. Continue routine management with her usual care team.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Continue routine management with her usual care team.
